description: Documentation corpus for this service. One markdown file per surface or concept, in docs/. This index is what search_docs ranks over; read_doc returns a file's contents.

docs.title: Agents
docs.summary: An agent is a definition, not a process: a prompt, a set of tools, a model, and optionally memory. Running it produces a [run](sessions-and-runs.md).
headings: What an agent is made of

docs.title: Agent inheritance
docs.summary: An agent can extend another: start from its prompt, tools, model and the rest, and declare only what is different. A system agent can be a parent, never a child.
headings: What is inherited and what is not
Setting, changing and pinning the parent
The guard on a parent's change

docs.title: Chat
docs.summary: The front door. Talk to any agent in the workspace directly; no node, no task, no setup.
headings: What you can point it at

docs.title: The CLI
docs.summary: `ah` drives the service from a terminal: the same operations as the dashboard, either in this process or over REST against the local backend. Command groups for every entity, commands generated from the OpenAPI schema, `ah api` as the raw escape hatch, and a single-file binary for REST mode.
headings: Two ways it reaches the service

docs.title: Declarative files: ah apply
docs.summary: Agents, deployments and memory pools declared in files in a repository; `ah apply` prints a plan (create, update, unchanged, drift, delete) and makes the hub match, recording hub ids in an `ah.lock` so the next apply updates instead of duplicating. Drift detection, `--prune`, `--export` from existing records.

docs.title: Connectors
docs.summary: Services this hub reaches out to: git providers (GitLab) and issue trackers (Jira), set up per workspace.

docs.title: Containers
docs.summary: Agents can run in-process or in Docker. Container mode isolates a run: its own filesystem view, its own network posture, its own lifetime.

docs.title: Deployments
docs.summary: Scheduled agent_task, flow and loop jobs shown as production deployments: the project, files, secrets and memory pools a job hands its runs, and a firing journal that shows whether each firing actually worked.

docs.title: Flows
docs.summary: A flow is a graph of agents run as one pipeline: nodes do work, edges define order, and the whole thing streams as it goes.

docs.title: Hooks and tool approval
docs.summary: Two ways to put a human, or the operator's own code, in front of a single tool call: hooks run around every call, and the approval gate holds a call until a person says yes.

docs.title: Imported agents
docs.summary: An agent that already exists, already works and has its own dependencies does not need rebuilding here. Import it from its git repository: the hub clones it, checks whether it can run, and adds it to the agent list either way.

docs.title: Installing and running the service
docs.summary: Three ways to run the service on your machine: Docker Compose from a checkout, the installer, and by hand. Then configuration, where state lives, upgrading, and what to check when it will not start.
headings: Path A: Docker Compose from a checkout
The first run in the browser

docs.title: Instances
docs.summary: An instance is a live copy of an agent: its own state, its own label, its own history. A resident instance is the one Run on an agent's page starts: a process or container of its own that answers its mailbox in several conversations and can take the agent's tasks.

docs.title: Loops
docs.summary: A loop wraps a [flow](flows.md) and re-runs it, feeding back a reviewer's complaints, until an agent judges the result good enough.

docs.title: Marketplace
docs.summary: The catalog of agents, flows and skills published across workspaces: how a thing built in one workspace gets published, cloned and used in another.
headings: Publishing an agent, a flow or a skill
When to reach for a published agent

docs.title: Agent templates
docs.summary: Ready single agents to start from in the create wizard: SRE agent, AI teammate, GitLab issue agent, invoice agent and contract review agent, each with a prompt, a safe tool set and a default outcome rubric.
headings: Why some channels are left out

docs.title: Memory
docs.summary: Agents have several complementary memory layers, bound to a pool. Core memory blocks are always in the prompt; the rest are ranked and fetched with tools. The pool is assigned per workspace, so the same agent can carry different knowledge in different workspaces. Personal memory is one private pool per workspace that the agents share, switched per workspace and per agent.

docs.title: Models
docs.summary: The Models page is the source of truth for which models exist, which are offered, what they cost, and which is default per provider.
headings: A first key switches on a model

docs.title: What this service is
docs.summary: An agent hub: a place to define AI agents, give them tools and memory, and run them, alone or in groups, against real work in a workspace.

docs.title: Projects
docs.summary: A project is one codebase or one effort inside a workspace. It gives work a folder, a structure graph and a task tree.
headings: What a project adds over a bare workspace

docs.title: Scheduling and the Plan page
docs.summary: Future work: notifications, agent tasks, flow and loop triggers, plus the inbox showing what fired.

docs.title: Service health and diagnostics
docs.summary: Whether the moving parts are alive, and what to do when they are not: the health snapshot, the /livez, /readyz and /metrics endpoints, and the doctor's checks.

docs.title: Sessions and runs
docs.summary: These two records are how everything in the product becomes observable. Why a run failed: its status, error and log, and what a stale run means.

docs.title: Settings
docs.summary: Credentials and connection details: provider keys and base URLs, local servers, custom backends, global temperature, agent execution, web access, RAG, logging, and the per-workspace palette. What models are offered and which is default lives on the [models](models.md) page, not here.

docs.title: Skills
docs.summary: Reusable procedures agents follow: steps or Markdown instructions, attached per agent, versioned with history, restore and pinning, installed copies that know when their original moved on, skills synced from any SKILL.md folder of a project repository, a safety review with flags, scripts and the license verdict on every imported skill, SKILL.md import and export.
headings: The part that trips everyone up

docs.title: System agents
docs.summary: An agent is either **system** (shipped with the product) or **custom** (yours). The roster lists the built-in agents and what each one does.
headings: What being a system agent means

docs.title: Tasks
docs.summary: A task is tracked work: it has a status, an owner, subtasks, dependencies, and a result that outlives the conversation that produced it.

docs.title: Issue trackers
docs.summary: Jira, linked to a project and mirrored into its tasks. A sync is idempotent: issues from the tracker become tasks. Tools read issues, create them, comment and transition their status.

docs.title: Teams
docs.summary: A team is a bounded roster of agents that know each other and work over a shared message board.

docs.title: Tools and capabilities
docs.summary: Tools are granted to an agent by name. Nothing is granted by default, including the calculator. run_code, a sandboxed code interpreter in a throwaway container, lives here too.
headings: Why capabilities and not tool names
Lifting the block: per agent, or for every agent
When a chat turn is refused
Delegation counts as holding the capability
What comes back from a delegate
Approval gates, which are a different thing

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.summary: Symptoms in the order people hit them: runs that will not start, output that never appears, numbers that look wrong, Docker, and the CLI.

docs.title: Views and Studio
docs.summary: A view is something an agent built to be looked at: a chart, a graph, a table, a 3D scene, a simulation, a slide deck (with layouts, themes, PDF and PowerPoint export) or a document.

docs.title: Web requests
docs.summary: Every page an agent fetched from the web (`fetch_url`), recorded with the text it was actually handed. The **Web Requests** page is where you read them.

docs.title: Workspaces
docs.summary: A workspace is the unit of isolation: its own folder on disk, its own roster of agents, its own settings, its own memory pools and its own projects.

docs.title: Workspace roles
docs.summary: A role is a kind of work (coder, reviewer, researcher, visualizer and more) and each workspace says which of its agents does it. System agents call @coder rather than swe_agent, so swapping in an imported agent such as Aider is one setting.

docs.title: Notifications
docs.summary: The in-app inbox (the bell) and the alert rules that raise a notification when a run fails or spend goes over a limit.

docs.title: Deploying for high availability
docs.summary: How to run the service on your machine with Docker Compose: backend and frontend, ports and the bind address, and releases, upgrading and rolling back with SQLite.

docs.title: Backup and recovery
docs.summary: ah db backup writes one archive (a self-contained SQLite file plus, by default, the state directories beside it); ah db restore loads it back; ah db verify checks it without touching the live database.

docs.title: Secrets
docs.summary: Encrypted per-workspace values, optionally scoped to one agent and bound to hosts, handed to a run as environment variables only under the names its agent declares.

docs.title: The demo workspace
docs.summary: A workspace called demo, seeded end to end: a small sample web shop, four custom agents, a flow, a loop, a paused weekly schedule, a team, views including a slide deck, tasks in every status and six recorded chats. Turned on with --with-demo or a Settings toggle.

docs.title: Terminal
docs.summary: A shell in a running container from the dashboard: a Docker run's container from the run page. Opened with a one-time ticket over a WebSocket; the hub keeps the shell through a dropped socket for a grace period and replays recent output on reconnect.

docs.title: Tool policy
docs.summary: Three modes decide what an agent's tool call can do: always_allow runs it, always_ask holds it for approval, and auto sends it to a small model to classify.
headings: What happens to a denied call

docs.title: Outcomes
docs.summary: A task can have an outcome: a markdown rubric that defines done, with max attempts, an optional grader model and an optional pass threshold.

docs.title: Steering
docs.summary: Send a message to a running run while it is still working, either injected into the conversation stream or interrupting it to restart on a new task.

docs.title: Agent loop
docs.summary: What happens between a run's model calls and the policies inside it: steering, compaction, tool search, structured output and fallback models, with guardrails and the tool policy around them, their agent and workspace settings, and the loop block a run records.

docs.title: Guardrails
docs.summary: Workspace or global checks on a run's input and final answer, by a rule (regex, keywords, PII, length) or a judge model, that block the run or warn, with an event log.

docs.title: Handoffs
docs.summary: Give a chat conversation to another agent: targets, history filters (full, summary, last_n, none), limits, events, and handoff versus delegation.

docs.title: Sandboxes
docs.summary: Where run_code and the Chat code panel run snippets: a throwaway docker container with no network by default, or a plain local subprocess as an explicit fallback, chosen by CODE_RUNNER_PROVIDER.
headings: The `run_code` tool and the code view

docs.title: Workspace files
docs.summary: Files uploaded once and referenced by id in chat, memory and tasks, plus numbered RAG citations in answers.
